title: Remark
body_md:
In the case of Giaquinta's example we have $p_1 = \dots = p_{n-1} = 2$, $p_n = 4$. For (1.6) we need 
$n \le 4$, which is in correspondence to the regularity result of \cite{CMM2009}. 
We do not know, if for the particular density $f$ from (1.1) the Liouville property is true in dimension 5.

title: Remark
body_md:
Now we want to replace (1.3) by the requirement that
\[
\lambda_i (1+t^2)^{\frac{p_i-2}{2}} \le f_i''(t) \le \Lambda_i (1+t^2)^{\frac{p_i-2}{2}} \quad t \in \mathbb{R}
\]
holds for the functions $f_i$ (nondegenerate case). The result of Theorem 1.1 does not extend to this different setting: (1.6) has to be replaced by the stronger condition $n \le 4$, and in Remark 1.3 one has to work with the value $\beta = \frac{1}{2}(4-n)$ instead of (1.8), which means that the exponents $p_i \ge 2$, $i = 1, \dots, n$, do not explicitly occur. The interested reader is referred to the forthcoming paper \cite{BF_forth}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Clearly (2.3) follows from (2.2) by Young's inequality. For (2.2) we observe
\[
\int_{\operatorname{spt}(\eta)} D^2 f( 
abla v) ig(
abla \partial_i v,
abla[ \eta^2 \partial_i v \, \Phi(\partial_i v)] ig) \, dx = 0
\]
and therefore
 egin{eqnarray*}
\lefteqn{\int_{\operatorname{spt}(\eta)} D^2 F(
abla v)(
abla \partial_i v, 
abla \partial_i v) \eta^2 \Phi(\partial_i v) \, dx} \
&&+ \int_{\operatorname{spt}(\eta)} D^2 F(
abla v)(
abla \partial_i v, 
abla \partial_i v) \eta^2 \Phi'(\partial_i v) \partial_i v \, dx \
&= &-2 \int_{\operatorname{spt}(
abla \eta)} D^2 F(
abla v)(
abla \partial_i v, 
abla \eta) \eta \partial_i v \, \Phi(\partial_i v) \, dx.
\end{eqnarray*}
By (2.1) we have that $\partial_i v \, \Phi'(\partial_i v) \ge 0$, hence
 egin{align*}
&\int_{\operatorname{spt}(\eta)} D^2 F(
abla v)(
abla \partial_i v, 
abla \partial_i v) \eta^2 \Phi(\partial_i v) \, dx \le \
&-2 \int_{\operatorname{spt}(
abla \eta)} D^2 F(
abla v)(
abla \partial_i v, 
abla \eta) \eta \partial_i v \, \Phi(\partial_i v) \, dx.
\end{align*}
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (in terms of the bilinear form $D^2 F(
abla v)$) on the right-hand side of the last inequality and applying Hölder's inequality (observing that $\Phi \ge 0$ during the calculations), we get (2.2).
